class_name: 対象-取り上げ-ニカケテ類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

glosses: when it comes to; as far as … goes
patterns.usage_note: Singles out a skill or field and rates someone inside it: the noun names the domain and what follows is almost always a superlative or an unmatched claim (料理にかけては一番だ, 右に出る者がいない). The sibling entries are the stretch from one point to another (夕方から夜にかけて) and staking something precious on a vow (名誉にかけて). The は-marked にかけては is the usual form, and the rating it carries is an extreme one, usually praise.

examples.ruby: 暗記[あんき]にかけては、姉[あね]に勝[か]てる気[き]がしない。
examples.english: When it comes to memorizing things, I don't stand a chance against my sister.

examples.ruby: 掃除[そうじ]にかけては父[ちち]の右[みぎ]に出[で]る者[もの]がいない。
examples.english: When it comes to cleaning, nobody can hold a candle to my dad.

examples.ruby: 水泳[すいえい]にかけては、部[ぶ]の誰[だれ]にも負[ま]けない自信[じしん]がある。
examples.english: When it comes to swimming, I'm sure I won't lose to anyone on the team.

patterns.usage_note: Puts up something the speaker holds precious (命, 名誉, 名, プライド, 面子) as the pledge behind what follows, so the clause is a vow, a hard resolve, or a flat denial: 神にかけて誓う, 命にかけて守る. The sibling entries are the stretch from one point to another (夕方から夜にかけて) and singling out a field of ability (暗記にかけては). Adding も raises the stakes and is optional, and the wording is earnest and somewhat literary.

examples.ruby: 名誉[めいよ]にかけて、この事件[じけん]は必[かなら]ず解決[かいけつ]する。
examples.english: On my honor, I will crack this case, whatever it takes.

examples.ruby: 職人[しょくにん]の意地[いじ]にかけても、途中[とちゅう]では投[な]げ出[だ]さない。
examples.english: My pride as a craftsman won't let me walk away half-finished.

examples.ruby: 母[はは]の名[な]にかけて、嘘[うそ]は言[い]っていない。
examples.english: I swear on my mother's name, I'm not lying.

glosses: once you put it in the hands of …
patterns.usage_note: Hands something over to a named expert or apparatus, after which an outcome that would otherwise be hard follows as a matter of course (名医にかけると, 校閲にかけると), so the main clause reports an effortless or surprising result. The noun must be one かける itself selects: 医者, 機械, 裁判, 校閲. It is bookish, and contemporary Japanese usually uses 〜にかかると or 〜の手にかかると; にかけますと is the polite variant.

examples.ruby: 名医[めいい]にかけると、どんな病[やまい]も治[なお]ってしまう。
examples.english: Put a patient in the hands of a top doctor and any illness simply clears up.

examples.ruby: あの機械[きかい]にかけますと、贋作[がんさく]もすぐに露見[ろけん]します。
examples.english: Run a piece through that machine and a forgery comes to light at once.

examples.ruby: どんな原稿[げんこう]も校閲[こうえつ]にかけると、誤字[ごじ]が山[やま]ほど出[で]る。
examples.english: Put any manuscript through proofreading and typos turn up by the dozen.
